# Finding Pairs $(a,b)$ with $ab + a + b = 2026$ and $\gcd(a,b) = 1$

## Setting Up the Factorization

I add 1 to both sides and factor:

$$ab + a + b + 1 = 2027 \implies (a+1)(b+1) = 2027$$

## Checking if 2027 is Prime

I test all primes up to $\lfloor\sqrt{2027}\rfloor = 45$:

| Divisor | Result |
|---------|--------|
| 2, 3, 5 | Fails (2027 is odd, digit sum 11, doesn't end in 0/5) |
| 7, 11, 13 | $7\times289=2023$, $11\times184=2024$, $13\times156=2028$ — none work |
| 17, 19, 23 | $17\times119=2023$, $19\times107=2033$, $23\times88=2024$ — none work |
| 29, 31, 37 | $29\times70=2030$, $31\times65=2015$, $37\times55=2035$ — none work |
| 41, 43 | $41\times49=2009$, $43\times47=2021$ — none work |

**2027 is prime.**

## Conclusion

Since 2027 is prime, its only factorization into two positive integers is $1 \times 2027$. This would force $a+1=1$ (i.e., $a=0$), which violates the requirement that $a$ be a positive integer.

$$\boxed{\text{There are no such pairs.}}$$
